title: August 8, 2026
tagline: Debriefing Thursday's meetup · Running out of steam

sections.heading: Debriefing Thursday's meetup
sections.body:
Two days out, the learnings from the meetup are worth writing down separately from the event itself.

Small rooms are my format. Seven people turned out to be structurally better than two hundred would have been: nobody can hide, there are no formed groups to break into, and the distance between attending and presenting was one sentence to the host. The tiny meetup that looked like a dud on paper was the better room. That changes how I pick events.

Organizers are starved for presenters — confirmed firsthand, since three of hers ghosted in one night. The application to demo at the August 19 event isn't a long shot; it's filling a need.

And the way the demo happened matters. I couldn't have stood up as self-promotion. But the host had a problem and I could solve it, so as a favor it was easy. Helping is apparently my native route to visibility.

The prediction ledger now has two entries. The Facebook post: predicted embarrassment, got five reactions and nothing unpleasant. The meetup: predicted a crowded room and a fumbled contact-exchange moment, got seven people and one rough stretch in the first ten minutes that dissolved on its own. Both times the fear front-loaded and was wrong about everything after minute ten.

sections.heading: Running out of steam
sections.body:
Also today: I told Claude I was considering abandoning the month's schedule entirely. A month was probably too long to schedule for me, I felt scatterbrained, and I'd run out of steam. My vote was to start fresh.

Per the rule I set on July 27, the urge got written down instead of acted on. The no-pivot commitment was made precisely for this moment — we predicted in advance that a restart would start sounding reasonable around now, and here it was, a little early and dressed as tidiness. The counterproposal on the table: keep the direction, keep August 26 as the day we read the numbers, and kill the heavy apparatus instead — the weekly documents, the day-by-day blocks, the ledger of what slipped. The plan may not be the problem. The tracking machinery, and being tired, might be.

Left it there for the weekend. Deciding while exhausted is how the last plan died.
